'''Edgardo Dizon Gomez''', {{post-nominals|post-noms=[[National Scientist of the Philippines|ONS]]}} (November 7, 1938 – December 1, 2019)<ref>{{cite news|title=National Scientist Edgardo Gomez, coral reef conservation champion, dies|url=https://www.rappler.com/philippines/246291-national-scientist-edgardo-gomez-dies/|date=December 3, 2019|access-date=December 3, 2019|publisher=[[Rappler]]}}</ref> was a Filipino biologist who was conferred the rank of [[National Scientist of the Philippines]] in 2014.<ref name=award>{{Cite news|url = http://newsinfo.inquirer.net/628386/aquino-confers-awards-on-four-new-national-scientists|title = Who are the 4 new National Scientists of PH|last = Sabillo|first = Kristine Angeli|date = August 12, 2014|accessdate = August 25, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url = http://www.msi.upd.edu.ph/?attachment_id=1884|title = National Scientist Dr. Edgardo D. Gomez|date = August 14, 2014|accessdate = August 25, 2014|publisher = UP Marine Science Institute|archive-date = March 3, 2016|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160303225224/http://www.msi.upd.edu.ph/?attachment_id=1884|url-status = dead}}</ref> He was a professor emeritus for marine biology at the [[University of the Philippines]] [[Marine Science Institute, University of the Philippines|Marine Science Institute]].

== Education and career ==
Gomez obtained his bachelor's degree in education, major in English and Social Science (''[[summa cum laude]]'') from [[De La Salle University]], his master's degree in [[biological science|Biology]] as a [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright Travel Grantee]] from [[St. Mary's University of Minnesota]] and Ph.D. degree in [[Marine biology|Marine Biology]] from [[University of California, San Diego]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url = http://www.nast.ph/index.php?option=com_profile&id=27&view=details&template=nast3&Itemid=20|title = Gomez, Edgardo D.|accessdate = August 25, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140827003200/http://www.nast.ph/index.php?option=com_profile&id=27&view=alldetails&template=nast3&Itemid=20|archive-date=August 27, 2014|publisher= National Academy of Science and Technology, Philippines}}</ref> He was the founding director of the [[Marine Science Institute, University of the Philippines|Marine Science Institute]] at the [[University of the Philippines Diliman]] upon his return in 1973 after his doctorate studies.

== Contributions ==
Gomez saw the need to protect the Philippine archipelago's vast marine resources in particular that of [[coral reef]]s. He led the world's first national-scale assessment of damage to coral reefs leading to international conservation initiatives such as the replanting of corals.<ref name="award" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url = http://newsinfo.inquirer.net/637793/sea-lover-with-positive-attitude-sees-hope-for-reefs-marine-life#ixzz3Drh83GhT|title = Sea lover with positive attitude sees hope for reefs, marine life|date = September 14, 2014|accessdate = September 20, 2014|publisher = Philippine Daily Inquirer|last = Pazzibugan|first = Dona}}</ref> He also pioneered [[giant clam]] (''Tridacna gigas'') breeding stationed in [[Bolinao, Pangasinan|Bolinao]] and other protective areas for coastal communities of the Philippines.<ref name="award" /><ref name=":2" />

Additionally, he took part in creating the baseline map of the Philippines, and provided information to the Philippine government during talks over the [[Spratly Islands dispute|territorial disputes in the Spratly Islands]].<ref name="award" /> In 2007, he pioneered the study on [[ocean acidification]] caused by increased levels of absorbed carbon dioxide in the ocean.<ref name=":1" />

Gomez was conferred the rank of [[National Scientist of the Philippines]] in 2014 by [[Benigno Aquino III]], the [[President of the Philippines]]. This award, which comes with a lifetime pension, has been bestowed upon over thirty leading scientists. The confirmation ceremony took place at the Rizal Hall of the [[Malacañan Palace]] where Gomez was awarded for his research and conservation efforts in invertebrate biology and ecology on 12 August 2014.<ref name=award/>

== Awards and recognition ==
* ''Laureate'' in the United Nations' Environmental Programme's (UNEP) Global 500 Roll of Honour in 1989
* The Outstanding Filipinos (TOFIL) Award for Science (Marine Biology) in 1992<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url = http://tofil.ph/greatleaders.php?id=46|title = Great Leaders in Our Midst|accessdate = August 25, 2014|last = Plata|first = Karen}}</ref>
* Academician by the [[National Academy of Science and Technology]] (NAST) in 1993
* Presidential Lingkod Bayan Awardee in 2000
* Pew Marine Conservation Fellow in 2001
* [[National Scientist of the Philippines]] for Marine Biology in 2014
* [[Asian Scientist 100]], ''[[Asian Scientist]]'', 2021
* On April 22, 2024, the [[Marine Science Institute, University of the Philippines|Marine Science Institute]], in its 50th founding anniversary, was re-named Edgardo D. Gomez Hall. The Marine Biodiversity Resources and Information System (MBRIS) building was inaugurated containing “MSI reference collections of marine organisms, libraries of natural products extracted from these organisms and other marine biodiversity collections,” MSI professor Maria Celia Malay announced.<ref>{{cite news |last1= Servallos |first1=Neil Jayson  |title=UP-Diliman renames marine science building|url=https://www.philstar.com/nation/2024/04/22/2349454/diliman-renames-marine-science-building |accessdate=April 22, 2024 |publisher= [[The Philippine Star]]|date=April 22, 2024}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Gomez was married to career ambassador Phoebe Abaya.  They have a son, Jose Edgardo Jr.
